solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inside information worried armed French policeman

indicators.note: something worried is shaken about, so the letters of 'armed' are jumbled

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for the facts or the lowdown
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip-off has rattled a gun-carrying officer in France.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'worried' shakes up ARMED behind it to make GENDARME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the armed police force serving in France, so the word names exactly that officer.

clue.text: Blot out imperfect pieces, about fifty

indicators.note: an imperfect version is not in its proper form, so the letters of 'pieces' are disordered
the jumbled 'pieces' sit about, that is around, the numeral for fifty

parts.note: the six letters rearranged
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone is erasing flawed bits of work, roughly fifty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperfect pieces' looks like the thing being blotted out, but 'pieces' is only the anagram fodder around the fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to obscure it or hide it from view, as the moon does the sun, a verb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Style of architecture in Finland, or Iceland

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters across 'Finland, or Iceland'

parts.note: the tail of Finland, the whole of 'or' and the start of Iceland

explanation.surface: A building style that might be Finnish or Icelandic, as if Nordic design were meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Nordic countries point toward Scandinavian design, but the answer runs across finlanD OR Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the oldest and plainest of the classical Greek column orders, a recognised architectural style.

clue.text: Regret is genuine after losing time

indicators.note: the word for genuine is taken after it loses the abbreviation for time

parts.note: genuine means true
T is the standard abbreviation for time, and it is dropped

explanation.surface: Real remorse sets in once the moment has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE without its T leaves RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to be sorry about it, an old verb and noun still common in 'rue the day'.

clue.text: Passing maple, here in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters of 'maple, here' are put in a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strolls past a maple tree at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot, but split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange MAPLE HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral lasts only a short while, so it is passing or fleeting, an adjective like the clue word.

clue.text: Fish only

definitions.meaning: a flatfish prized in European cooking, the Dover variety especially
only in the sense of single or lone, as in the one survivor

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat marine species and the adjective meaning single or lone happen to be spelt identically.

clue.text: Extra, and almost certain, advantage

indicators.note: almost the whole word for certain, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: sure means certain; its last letter goes
a plus is a point in your favour

explanation.surface: A list of three qualities: something additional, nearly sure, and beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its E to become SUR, then PLUS is added, giving SURPLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over beyond what is required, so as an adjective it means additional or spare.

clue.text: First of landlords to reduce rent

indicators.note: only the opening letter of 'landlords' is taken

parts.note: the initial letter
to ease is to lessen or reduce

explanation.surface: The first property owner decides to lower the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: L plus EASE gives LEASE; the surface makes 'rent' a noun, but the definition is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease a flat is to hire it for payment over a fixed term, the same verb sense as rent.

clue.text: Some crass, lurid aspersion

indicators.note: only some of the letters in 'crass, lurid' are used, a consecutive run

parts.note: the tail of crass and the start of lurid

explanation.surface: A coarse, sensational insult is thrown at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans crasS LURid.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging remark on someone's character, and a slur is exactly such an insulting attack.

clue.text: Very delicate eastern article, genuine

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east or eastern
the definite article
real means genuine

explanation.surface: An authentic, extremely fragile object from the East, such as fine porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: E, THE and REAL simply join to make ETHEREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something so light and refined it seems not of this world, hence extremely delicate.

clue.text: Wide range of toasted crumpets

indicators.note: toasting changes something's state, so the letters of 'crumpets' are altered in order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged; a crumpet is a British spongy griddle cake eaten toasted

explanation.surface: A café offers a big selection of toasted crumpets, the spongy British teatime griddle cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toasted' is exactly what one does to crumpets, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full span of values or kinds between two extremes, as in the political spectrum.

clue.text: Trustworthy agent on university board

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
U is the usual abbreviation for university
a board is a flat plank or table

explanation.surface: A reliable representative sits on a university's governing board.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts REP above U and TABLE, giving REPUTABLE; the board is furniture, not a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reputable has a good standing and can be relied upon, the same sense as trustworthy.

clue.text: Son leaving smooth vegetable

indicators.note: the son departs from the word for smooth, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy
S is the abbreviation for son, and it is removed

explanation.surface: A boy walks off with a smooth-skinned vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEEK loses its S to give LEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is a long green-and-white allium grown in gardens, one example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Leave suddenly, affected by low grades?

parts.note: D and E are poor marks in an exam
camp means exaggerated or affected in manner

explanation.surface: A student drops out abruptly, upset by poor marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' reads as upset by the grades, but it means mannered or theatrical; 'by' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart abruptly or secretly, often by night, which matches leaving suddenly.

clue.text: Train as mobile mechanic, perhaps

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters of 'train as' move about

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to qualify as a mechanic who travels to customers' cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a mechanic is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker or craftsperson, and a mechanic is one kind of such tradesperson.

clue.text: Stand down after head of state breaks rule

indicators.note: the initial of 'state' breaks into the word for rule, splitting it

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of 'state'

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A leader quits after the head of state defies the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes into REIGN, giving RE-S-IGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to give up an office or post voluntarily, which is what resigning means.

clue.text: The Spanish convict brought over on vessel

indicators.note: brought over means turned back, so 'the Spanish' and 'convict' run in the opposite direction

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish
an old lag is British slang for a long-serving prisoner
the word itself

explanation.surface: A Spanish prisoner is transported by ship, as convicts once were.
explanation.walkthrough: EL LAG turned back gives GALLE, then ON; the surface puts 'on vessel' together, but ON is just a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing ship, famously Spanish, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Loud turn, in reality

definitions.note: 'in reality' and 'in fact' are the same phrase

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a turn is a performer's act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A noisy stage performance that is actually true to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests rotating, but it is a stage turn, ACT, after F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something that truly exists or happened, so it belongs to reality rather than fiction.

clue.text: A quarrel involving thrower's last dart

parts.note: the article itself

indicators.note: 'a quarrel' involves, that is takes inside itself, the final letter of 'thrower's'

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument

indicators.note: only the closing letter of 'thrower's' is taken

parts.note: the final letter of thrower

explanation.surface: A pub argument breaks out over a player's final dart.
explanation.walkthrough: The R slips into A ROW to give A-R-ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart is a small pointed missile, and an arrow is a pointed projectile shot or thrown in the same way.

clue.text: Recount story that's revealing

parts.note: to recount is to narrate
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone narrates an anecdote that exposes a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: TELL plus TALE makes TELLTALE, used as an adjective as in a telltale sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign or blush gives away something hidden, so the adjective means betraying or exposing.

clue.text: Sat up eating father's light snacks

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for sat is read bottom to top
the turned-back word eats, that is swallows, the word for father

parts.note: the word itself, to be turned back
pa is an informal name for father

explanation.surface: Dad stayed up late munching small snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT reversed is TAS, which takes in PA to give TA-PA-S; 'Sat up' reads as staying awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury Spanish dishes served with drinks, which are indeed light snacks.

clue.text: Piece of the woodwork from pub on bridge

parts.note: to bridge a river is to cross it
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A bit of timber salvaged from a pub that stood on a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after. 'The woodwork' is British football commentators' slang for the goalposts and the beam joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal beam of a football goal, one part of what commentators call the woodwork.

clue.text: Cereal grass forming part of military experiment

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words 'military experiment' taken as a run

parts.note: the end of military and the start of experiment

explanation.surface: An army trial involving a grain crop.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans militaRY Experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a grain-bearing plant of the grass family grown for flour and whisky, so it is a cereal grass.

clue.text: One entering through wharf

indicators.note: 'one' enters, going inside, the word for through

parts.note: per means through or by way of, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone walks in by way of the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into PER, giving P-I-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a platform built out into water where boats tie up, much the same structure as a wharf.

clue.text: Whiskey in can, a double?

indicators.note: the letter for whiskey is placed in the word for can

parts.note: a tin is a can
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bar customer asks whether whiskey from a can counts as a double measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A double' looks like a drinks measure, but it is a lookalike; W goes into TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is someone who looks exactly like another person, and a twin is the classic example of that.

clue.text: Service still good around middle of morning

indicators.note: the words for still and good go around the central letter of 'morning'

parts.note: even so means still or nevertheless

indicators.note: only the central letter of the seven in 'morning' is taken

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A church service is still well attended by mid-morning.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes between EVEN SO and G to give EVENSONG; a morning service suggests matins, but the answer is an evening one.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, also called vespers, one kind of church service.
